title: MeitY partners with PhonePe to strengthen PM GatiShakti with granular data intelligence
body_text:
The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with PhonePe to draw on insights from PhonePe PulsePro, an enterprise data intelligence platform, to support the PM GatiShakti mission for national infrastructure planning, economic analysis, and holistic urban and rural development.
Under the MoU, PhonePe PulsePro metrics will be integrated into the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan portal, managed in collaboration with the Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics (BISAG-N). This will give government planners access to granular, hyperlocal transactional insights drawn from PhonePe's extensive digital transaction ecosystem, complementing existing datasets and supporting smarter, data-driven decisions for national development planning.
Sharing his views on the MoU, Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), said, "Data-driven intelligence can play an important role in enabling more informed planning and decision-making. The granular and hyperlocal insights available through PhonePe PulsePro can complement existing datasets and provide additional visibility into emerging trends across markets and geographies. We welcome PhonePe's initiative to make these insights available through the PM GatiShakti framework and support India's journey towards Viksit Bharat."
PhonePe PulsePro transforms aggregated and anonymised transaction data into hyperlocal insights, offering a granular view of trends across geographies, categories, and markets, and enabling organisations to identify emerging trends and derive actionable intelligence from real-world activity.
Commenting on the MoU, Karthik Raghupathy, Head of Strategy at PhonePe, said, "Since the launch of PhonePe Pulse, we have seen how transaction-led insights can help build a more nuanced understanding of markets and emerging trends. PhonePe PulsePro takes this intelligence further through granular, hyperlocal, and near-real-time market signals. By making these insights available to MeitY, we hope to contribute to a stronger data ecosystem and support more informed, evidence-based infrastructure planning. We are delighted to play our part in enabling the use of data for broader public good."
PhonePe Limited (formerly PhonePe Private Limited) is a technology company that builds digital platforms for Payments, Digital Distribution Services, and Financial Services.

enrichment.summary: MeitY signed an MoU with fintech company PhonePe to integrate data from PhonePe PulsePro, an enterprise data intelligence platform, into the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan portal. The tie-up, facilitated with BISAG-N which manages the portal, will give government planners access to granular, hyperlocal transaction-based insights to complement existing datasets for infrastructure and economic planning. MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan and PhonePe's Karthik Raghupathy both welcomed the partnership as supporting data-driven, evidence-based planning.
enrichment.context:
PM GatiShakti is the National Master Plan launched in 2021 to ensure integrated planning and coordinated execution of infrastructure projects across ministries by overlaying data from various departments (roads, railways, ports, etc.) on a single GIS-based platform managed with BISAG-N's technical support. A recurring challenge for such planning has been the lack of granular, real-time economic activity data at the local level, which is usually available only through periodic government surveys or census data with significant time lags.

This MoU represents a growing trend of government institutions partnering with private digital platforms to access anonymised, aggregated transactional data for public planning purposes, similar to earlier PhonePe Pulse reports that mapped digital payment trends across India. By feeding hyperlocal payment and market activity data into GatiShakti, planners could potentially identify emerging economic hubs, consumption patterns, or underserved areas more dynamically than traditional data sources allow. This reflects the broader push toward data-driven governance and the use of public-private data ecosystems to strengthen the 'Viksit Bharat' infrastructure and economic planning agenda, though it also raises considerations around data privacy, anonymisation standards, and the appropriate use of private commercial data in public policy decisions.
